analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts: scripts/test-ci-tested-tree.py and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. Neither touches provider runtime code, coordinator-provider wire handling, keys, attestation, cache storage or any threat-model asset (A-001..A-020, TB-002..TB-014, T-041). I found no security regression in these test changes.

test-ci-tested-tree.py (head lines 57-92, 128-135, 186-189) adds tests for squash-merge tree records (`tree_record`, `tree-name`). They pin that a tree-only record skips only when the tree matches, the components are covered, and the run succeeded in the same repository (no fork head repository) and on the same workflow path. They also pin that a pull request never matches a tree-only record with a mismatched base. These assertions look conservative. The lookup implementation, scripts/ci-tested-tree.py, is not supplied. Its handling of tree-only records, including whether a PR-run artifact could be reused for an unrelated push, is unverified. That is a CI-integrity concern outside the provider threat model.

test-darkbloom-route.py pins workflow shape and router behaviour:
- `build-*` lanes now follow `requested()` only. The `BUILT` push-refresh case is dropped, and GPU lanes use `cluster_gpu`.
- MAX_ATTEMPTS defaults to 6, validated 1-9, with exponential backoff and Retry-After handling.
- The hourly workflow is removed.
- A new `unlabel` job on literal ubuntu-24.04 holds the only issues/pull-requests write. Tests assert it has no `uses:`, secrets or checkout, and that no other job holds issues/pull-requests write.
- The stranded-run jq logic is hardened so partially completed Darkbloom attempts are not cancelled.
- Blacksmith or ubuntu-24.04 runners are allowed in the no-route workflows.

These tests tighten or maintain least privilege. The workflow YAML files they pin (ci-dev.yml, ci-master.yml, darkbloom-route.yml, provider-plan.yml, the watchdog) are not in this batch. Their actual permissions and the correctness of the label-consumption `unlabel` job need review in the batch containing the workflows. The 160s timeout and retry loop are availability concerns only.
